transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-08
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Sarah Kim (CTO, Brookside), Alex Gomez (Head of Infra), Priya Singh (Security Architect)
---
[00:00] Nina Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm nina, i'm the AE on the account. marcus is our se who will run the bench marks, and from brookside?
[00:15] Dr. Sarah Kim: hi, sarah here. thanks, keeping it short, we've got a security pilot to validate redwood for clinical notes summarization and triage workflows.
[00:30] Alex Gomez: alex - infra. we care about latency and also keeping PHI in our control, so VPC/private deployment options matter.
[01:20] Marcus Lee: great, high level agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan, security requirements (soc two, iso, sso), and timelines. apologies if my mic pops.
[02:15] Priya Singh: for us, the must-haves are: SOC 2 report, ISO 27001 cert, SSO/SAML with SCIM for provisioning, RBAC at route and token level, KMS integration (HSM optional), and immutable audit logs with at least 1 year retention. also we need evidence of encryption at rest and in transit.
[03:05] Nina Patel: totally understood. we can provide SOC 2 type II and ISO artifacts. we support SAML SSO and SCIM, RBAC is available in console for roles/teams, and audit logs are exported to your SIEM or stored in S3 with configurable retention. i will send the specific docs after the call.
[04:00] Dr. Sarah Kim: can you clarify private deployment vs hosted? we prefer private control plane or VPC peering so keys never leave our network.
[04:40] Marcus Lee: right. Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC/on-prem). for the pilot we can do a VPC peered private deployment or a dedicated instance with strict network controls. note: dedicated may be faster to spin up for pilot but private gives more control over key management.
[05:30] Alex Gomez: what's the timeline to get a private deployment up for a 4-week pilot?
[05:50] Nina Patel: typically 2-3 weeks for VPC setup and inventory review, assuming approvals. dedicated can be provisioned faster, ~1 week. for planning let's assume 2 weeks prep then 4-week pilot.
[06:30] Priya Singh: bench marks — we want p50 and p95 latencies, throughput (req/s), token/sec cost, and memory footprint. also regression tests on quality for prompts.
[07:00] Marcus Lee: yes, our benchmark plan: we'll run an initial synthetic workload that approximates your real traffic. can you share expected concurrent sessions and avg tokens per request?
[07:30] Alex Gomez: typical peak is ~120 concurrent clinicians using the tool, average request ~600 tokens, bursty during shift changes. daily token volume around 10-12 million tokens.
[08:00] Marcus Lee: OK that maps to roughly 100-150 req/s under peak. for the pilot we'll scale to 150 req/s and capture p50/p95 and cost-per-token. target p50 < 200ms and p95 < 600ms for the interactive flow, but we'll validate.
[09:00] Dr. Sarah Kim: what's the model variants and quantization options? we want to balance cost vs accuracy.
[09:25] Marcus Lee: we can test a few open models we vet on Redwood, and we have quantized variants for lower-cost runs. model routing for failover is available; caching of prefixes/K V cache reduces cost for repeated prompts, though the transcript system sometimes shows KV as K V cash in logs.
[10:00] Priya Singh: audit trail — we need comments on who accessed what patient data and model outputs, and the logs must be tamper-evident. retention 12 months, exportable to our SIEM.
[10:40] Nina Patel: audit logs include token-level traces, per-request metadata, user-id mapping via SSO. they can be sent to your CloudWatch/Datadog/Splunk or S3. we support log signing for tamper evidence and can discuss HSM-backed signing if needed.
[12:00] Alex Gomez: on encryption, we want customer-managed keys (CMK) in our KMS/HSM. can Redwood work with that?
[12:25] Marcus Lee: yes, Private supports KMS integrations; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer keys via HSM in some enterprise tiers. we'll note exact flows in the doc.
[14:00] Dr. Sarah Kim: success criteria for pilot? what are we agreeing to measure?
[14:25] Nina Patel: proposed success criteria: 1) functional — model outputs meet the clinical accuracy thresholds on your evaluation prompts; 2) security — all compliance checks (SOC 2 evidence, SSO provisioning, RBAC, audit logs export) validated by your security team; 3) performance — p50/p95 and throughput within agreed SLOs; 4) integration — SSO + provisioning + key management validated; 5) cost — unit cost within target.
[15:30] Priya Singh: we will provide an eval set and pass/fail thresholds for accuracy; security validation is a hard gate.
[16:15] Marcus Lee: good. benchmark specifics: we'll run three passes — baseline (no quantization), quantized, and caching-enabled. capture p50/p95, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost estimates.
[18:00] Alex Gomez: do you have example numbers we can expect for cost per 1M tokens on dedicated vs hosted?
[18:30] Nina Patel: ballpark - hosted higher variability, dedicated lowers unit cost by ~20-40% depending on utilization; exact numbers depend on model and quantization. we'll include a pricing spreadsheet.
[20:00] Dr. Sarah Kim: legal will want data residency and retention controls spelled out.
[20:20] Nina Patel: note we can pin region and provide contract language for data residency, plus retention controls in console. we'll share a draft DPA and security playbook.
[22:00] Priya Singh: about SAML - we need SCIM for user provisioning and attribute mapping to match our roles. can you map groups to RBAC policies?
[22:35] Marcus Lee: yes, SCIM + SAML supported; group-to-role mapping is configurable. we'll demo mapping in the setup call. sometimes our docs show S S O spelled oddly but it's supported.
[24:00] Alex Gomez: operational concern — fallback if capacity constrained. we need graceful degradation paths and model routing policies.
[24:25] Marcus Lee: Redwood has routing policies and fallbacks to compatible model variants and region-level fallback to keep the app online. we can configure canary rollouts and A/B for safety.
[26:00] Dr. Sarah Kim: timeline recap?
[26:20] Nina Patel: propose: Nina sends SOC2/ISO + pricing (by 2027-04-12). Marcus will run initial benchmark and send workload sizing sheet (by 2027-04-15). Priya to confirm security contacts (by 2027-04-14). If approved, provision dedicated or VPC in week of 2027-04-19 and begin 4-week pilot.
[28:00] Priya Singh: one more - we need to run a small compliance checklist before pilot start; can you send the checklist?
[28:20] Nina Patel: yes, we'll include a compliance checklist in the packet.
[30:00] Marcus Lee: on the benchmark run, can you share a sample prompt set and any redaction rules? we'll need to mask PHI during synthetic runs and also run a parallel run with anonymized real data per your DPA.
[31:10] Alex Gomez: we'll provide an anonymized dataset and the prompt templates.
[33:00] Dr. Sarah Kim: are there any constraints around SOC 2 scoping — e.g., do we need vendor audits or self-attestations?
[33:30] Nina Patel: we typically share our SOC 2 type II report and supporting attestations; for more in-depth vendor audits we can arrange an enterprise security review and provide additional artifacts under an NDA.
[35:00] Priya Singh: can we get a sample of audit logs schema?
[35:20] Marcus Lee: yes, will attach sample log schema and a sample export to S3 in the follow-up. the logs include request id, user id, model id, tokens in/out, timestamps, and hashes for tamper-evidence. sometimes transcription picks up model id as model eye, ignore that.
[36:40] Alex Gomez: anything on SLA?
[37:00] Nina Patel: for Dedicated/Private enterprise tiers we include SLA commitments. we'll include a summary of uptime and latency SLOs in the packet.
[38:00] Dr. Sarah Kim: ok, good. can you also provide a runbook for incident response and data breach notifications?
[38:20] Nina Patel: yes, incident response playbook and contact list will be provided.
[40:00] Marcus Lee: i'll propose the benchmark schedule: Day 0 - provisioning, Day 1 - baseline, Day 3 - quantized, Day 5 - caching, Day 7 - integration tests with SSO/SCIM, then a week of steady-state sim. results by 2027-04-15.
[42:30] Priya Singh: that works. we'll review results and convene compliance group.
[44:00] Nina Patel: thanks everyone, i'll send the packet with SOC2/ISO, pricing, bench sheet, compliance checklist. any final questions?
[44:30] Dr. Sarah Kim: not from me. thanks.
---
Recap & Next Steps included above. Shared artifacts to follow: SOC 2 + ISO artifacts, pricing spreadsheet, benchmark plan and workload sizing sheet, audit log schema sample, DPA draft, compliance checklist.
